title: Arjuna stands firm
hook: Nani's one note, and how Arjuna's story ends
carry: krishna teaches, then leaves the choice to arjuna
tomorrow: Nani won't just say the verse. she sings it. why?

segments.voice: Yesterday, shruti: the holy word is heard first, and Maitreyi, who turned down the whole earth to ask what lasts. Today, the two weeks come back, and Arjuna's story gets its ending.

After the birthday, a kitchen, late. The card is propped against the fruit bowl. The granddaughter reads the line aloud to her grandmother, slowly, dandas and all. Nani doesn't correct a single sound. She has one note: now say it like you're telling me, not reading to me. It might be the whole point, because the Gita itself began as words told, friend to friend, in a chariot.
screen: `THE WHOLE LINE, OUT LOUD.` → `NOT ONE SOUND CORRECTED.` → `SAY IT LIKE YOU'RE TELLING ME.`

segments.voice: Remember where this began: Arjuna's bow slipping from his hand, Arjuna sitting down and saying, I will not fight. Krishna answers him across eighteen chapters. The act is yours, never the fruit. No one stops acting, so make every act an offering. And near the very end, Krishna does something surprising. He doesn't command. He says: I've told you this wisdom; reflect on it fully, then do as you choose. Then he asks: have you heard this with a focused mind? Is your confusion gone? And Arjuna answers: my confusion is gone, my memory has come back, my doubts are cleared; I stand firm, and I'll do as you say. That's the shape of the Gita, and many teachers say it's part of why Hindus love it: a teaching given by a friend, heard, thought through, and then chosen. Look at everything these two weeks held to get one line said well. Ganesha writing only what he understood. Om before the prayer. Speech that's true and kind. A word heard before it's read. Nani's note gathers them up: the line isn't for reading at someone. It's for telling, the way Krishna told it, to someone you love, and then living by.
screen: `EIGHTEEN CHAPTERS LATER.` · `REFLECT FULLY, THEN CHOOSE.` · `MY CONFUSION IS GONE. I STAND FIRM.` · `TOLD, HEARD, THOUGHT THROUGH, CHOSEN.`

segments.voice: Pick one line you love, from a prayer, a verse, a song, and say it aloud once as if reading it off a page. Then say it again as if you were telling it to someone sitting right across from you, someone you'd want it to help. Sit with the difference, and with the line, for the rest of the time.
The sounds: throat to lips, little breath and great, om before the prayer, heard first, and then said to someone.
For the road: Krishna teaches, then leaves the choice to Arjuna, and Arjuna stands. Two weeks, done.

howItsDone: Hindu children often learn a verse by hearing an elder or teacher say it, repeating it back, and only later reading it; a family member may correct the sounds and then, as Nani does here, the way it is said. Many teachers point to Gita 18.63 to show that the Gita ends by asking for reflection and free choice.
